Intrusion Detection and Prevention", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 100, 549, 119 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Maintaining Internet gateway security requires ongoing and comprehensive system operation, support and surveillance to oversee the prevention, detection, response and escalation of any irregular, abnormal or suspicious activities or incidents. This can be achieved by proper manual procedures such as reviewing and analysing log or statistics, and testing and drilling the incident handling procedures.", "bbox": [ 184, 142, 867, 228 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If possible, IDPS tools should be installed and used at strategic locations to collect and examine information continuously for suspicious activity. Both network based and host based IDPS tools could be used. The former type examines network packets in the network while the latter one monitors the system configuration and application activities on a single host system.", "bbox": [ 184, 248, 867, 332 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Improper configuration and use of these tools may disclose information to attackers and result in a false sense of security.", "bbox": [ 186, 353, 870, 388 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "IDPS tools should be used to identify suspicious activities on both the network and the host machines, in particular the web server and the mail server.", "bbox": [ 186, 412, 865, 445 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Automatic generation of notifications or alerts by electronic messages or mobile paging should be set up to warn system administrators when symptoms of attacks are detected.", "bbox": [ 186, 448, 877, 497 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If applicable, systems or functions capable of reacting to suspicious network activity should be implemented to disconnect or block these connections in the first place and record them for subsequent analysis.", "bbox": [ 186, 503, 867, 552 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• These tools should be properly tested and verified before going operation.", "bbox": [ 186, 557, 826, 573 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• The use, administration and management of these tools should be properly controlled and restricted.", "bbox": [ 186, 577, 831, 610 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Firewall system should be properly configured to protect and hide such tools as far as possible.", "bbox": [ 186, 615, 872, 647 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• The attack signature files should be kept up-to-date.", "bbox": [ 186, 653, 648, 669 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "New update of signature file and blocking rules should be tested thoroughly and verified before putting into production. The new update should be tested to determine whether its new / modified signature and blocking rules perform as expected, and whether it conflicts with the original signature and blocking rules.", "bbox": [ 186, 673, 878, 739 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Proper operating, administrative and monitoring procedures should be established for using these tools. The procedures should be reviewed periodically to ensure the network configuration is up-to-date.", "bbox": [ 186, 743, 796, 794 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "header", "text": "INTRUSION DETECTION AND PREVENTION", "bbox": [ 515, 55, 880, 70 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Internet Gateway Security", "bbox": [ 115, 915, 426, 931 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "Page 34", "bbox": [ 821, 915, 880, 931 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The strategic places for IDPS deployment could be on firewall, hosts or any information assets that are important. A secure Internet gateway could be introduced in the Internet Gateway infrastructure as a first line of defence deployed between the Internet and the existing Internet Gateway to fight against threats on the Internet. The secure Internet gateway could be configured by allowing intrusion detection and prevention in web filtering, https traffic inspection, malicious IP address and domain detection or blocking and monitoring of network traffic, detecting malware, and preventing information systems from infection.", "bbox": [ 184, 86, 877, 220 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "header", "text": "INTRUSION DETECTION AND PREVENTION", "bbox": [ 515, 55, 880, 70 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Internet Gateway Security", "bbox": [ 115, 915, 426, 931 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "Page 35", "bbox": [ 821, 915, 880, 931 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10. 216, 359, 236 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• All gateway components should be physically secured and be placed in a restricted area.", "bbox": [ 186, 258, 820, 292 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The computer room with these equipment placed should be well equipped to protect against physical or natural disasters.", "bbox": [ 186, 296, 848, 330 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Lockable racks should be used to store these components.", "bbox": [ 186, 334, 697, 350 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Regular monitor and review on the current physical protection e.g. examine site entrance or access logs, check cables for unauthorised taps, check door locks of racks and any sticking labels.", "bbox": [ 186, 355, 875, 404 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Remove and erase all storage media before disposal, especially those containing system configuration.", "bbox": [ 186, 408, 878, 442 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10.2 Logging", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 117, 465, 275, 486 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Enable logging functions wherever applicable in firewall, router, OS, web server and mail server.", "bbox": [ 186, 509, 882, 541 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Keep logs such as the error logs, system logs, access logs, web server and mail server logs with adequate storage capacity available.", "bbox": [ 186, 546, 867, 580 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Endeavor to log information such as invalid account login attempts, account misuse in websites, illegal or unauthorised attempts to websites, administrative and configuration updates, or specific information of requests, including requestor's IP address, host name, URL and names of files accessed.", "bbox": [ 186, 584, 868, 649 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Logs should be reviewed regularly and kept for at least a week in a secure place. \nWrite-once device such as optical disk may be used to record those log files.", "bbox": [ 186, 654, 877, 687 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Logs showing intrusions and attacks should be kept properly for investigation and record.", "bbox": [ 186, 691, 858, 724 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Consideration on privacy should be made when designing the types and details of information to be logged.", "bbox": [ 186, 728, 867, 762 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "header", "text": "OTHER SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS", "bbox": [ 564, 55, 880, 70 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Internet Gateway Security", "bbox": [ 115, 915, 426, 931 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "Page 36", "bbox": [ 821, 915, 880, 931 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10.3 Backup and Recovery", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 117, 86, 403, 106 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Formal backup and recovery procedures should be established and well documented.", "bbox": [ 186, 129, 806, 162 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "All gateway components' configuration, log files, system files, programs, data and other system information should be backed up regularly and whenever there is configuration change. Encryption may be applied to the backup if necessary.", "bbox": [ 186, 167, 878, 217 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Backup copies should be kept in a secure place. Two backup copies for system configuration are preferably to be kept with one on-site and one off-site.", "bbox": [ 186, 220, 872, 255 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10.4 Protection against Malware", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 117, 277, 453, 296 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Enable anti-malware protection or malware detection to check all incoming Internet traffic, and automatically clean for malware.", "bbox": [ 186, 320, 840, 355 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• The gateway should be configured to stop traffic with malicious content, quarantine / drop them, and create audit logs for future investigation.", "bbox": [ 186, 358, 816, 391 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Malware signature and definition should be updated regularly. The update should be configured as automatic and update frequency should be at least on daily basis.", "bbox": [ 186, 395, 855, 445 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If automatic update is not possible (e.g. mobile devices which are often not attached to networks), update should be done manually at least once a week.", "bbox": [ 186, 450, 845, 483 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Users should also note that from time to time, there could be ad-hoc and serious malware outbreaks. If so, users should follow the instructions and immediately update with the latest malware signature and definition in order to protect against malware outbreak. After signature/definition update, users should conduct full-system scan on the machines to detect any potential existence of the concerned malware.", "bbox": [ 186, 486, 873, 585 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Regularly perform malware scanning for the host machine where the information servers are installed.", "bbox": [ 186, 590, 786, 623 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10.5 Operating System Security", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 117, 646, 448, 666 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Operating system (OS), where the network application software are running on, should be carefully selected with respect to the security requirements. The vulnerabilities or security holes of the OS may affect the security of the application software.", "bbox": [ 184, 688, 867, 755 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "A secure OS platform should be chosen especially for the firewall and critical servers. It is preferable to select those OSs which can provide the following features:", "bbox": [ 186, 776, 821, 826 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Multiple simultaneous processes", "bbox": [ 186, 851, 494, 868 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Secure file access permissions and controls", "bbox": [ 186, 872, 579, 889 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "header", "text": "OTHER SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS", "bbox": [ 564, 55, 880, 70 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Internet Gateway Security", "bbox": [ 115, 915, 426, 931 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "Page 37", "bbox": [ 821, 915, 880, 931 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Accountability and auditability of users and system actions such as detailed event logs", "bbox": [ 186, 87, 840, 121 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Identification and authentication of all users on the system", "bbox": [ 186, 124, 704, 141 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Resources isolations such as controlling reuse of system objects e.g. deleted files, allocated memory", "bbox": [ 186, 146, 843, 179 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Different OSs have different ways to secure their configuration. Listed below are some examples for general reference.", "bbox": [ 186, 201, 853, 236 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Remove or disable all unnecessary services or processes, especially those unused but default running services and processes.", "bbox": [ 186, 258, 823, 293 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Remove unnecessary default accounts if possible, otherwise change all default accounts with strong passwords.", "bbox": [ 186, 296, 865, 330 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The number of privileged processes running should be reduced to the minimum. \nThe assignment of privileges should be carefully handled.", "bbox": [ 186, 333, 877, 368 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Default file permissions and privileges should be reviewed periodically, and set to restrictive values.", "bbox": [ 186, 371, 873, 403 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Use a strong password for the system administrator account. The password should be regularly changed.", "bbox": [ 186, 408, 840, 441 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Standardise and minimise the number of OS versions and software to make installation and maintenance more manageable.", "bbox": [ 186, 446, 838, 479 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Install OS upgrades regularly and apply latest OS patches, especially those related to security issues.", "bbox": [ 186, 483, 833, 516 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10.6 Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Network", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 117, 540, 460, 559 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Peer-to-peer (P2P) file-sharing systems are commonly characterised as networkbased applications in which the peers (i.e. the participating computers) use the Internet to exchange files with each other directly. P2P network is a network model used by the P2P file-sharing systems, such that every peer plays the roles of a client and a server at the same time. This opens a channel for files stored in an user computer in internal network to be uploaded to other peers in the Internet.", "bbox": [ 184, 581, 873, 682 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The potential security risks with P2P technology include:", "bbox": [ 186, 703, 655, 722 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Improper configuration may lead to information leakage when using a P2P application. Other files apart from the ones being shared can be exposed unknowingly if they are stored in the same workstation or storage media. Once a file is uploaded to the peers, this information is hard to be removed from the P2P network totally.", "bbox": [ 186, 744, 873, 827 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "P2P applications need the firewall to open a number of ports in order to function properly. Each open port in the firewall is a potential avenue that attackers might use to exploit the network.", "bbox": [ 186, 831, 880, 882 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "header", "text": "OTHER SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS", "bbox": [ 564, 55, 880, 70 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Internet Gateway Security", "bbox": [ 115, 915, 426, 931 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "Page 38", "bbox": [ 821, 915, 880, 931 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "As P2P networks facilitate file sharing among peers, malware can exploit this channel to propagate themselves to other peers.", "bbox": [ 186, 87, 857, 121 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• The P2P application may contain vulnerability that attacker may use for spreading malware, hacking or launching a denial of service attack.", "bbox": [ 186, 124, 811, 159 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "When a file is downloaded using a P2P software, it is not possible to know who created the file or whether it is trustworthy. The person downloading the file might be exposed to criminal and/or civil litigation if any illegal content is involved.", "bbox": [ 186, 161, 873, 228 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Use of P2P applications in B/Ds’ networks could generate large amount of network traffic, monopolising network bandwidth that impacts other important business applications.", "bbox": [ 186, 231, 867, 281 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "As P2P technology relies on user workstations, it is unmanageable from the server side aspect and all the security measures implemented at server side has no effect to such P2P sharing.", "bbox": [ 186, 286, 865, 336 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The best practices for mitigating the risks of P2P technology are listed below.", "bbox": [ 186, 358, 820, 376 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds should take very serious consideration in employing P2P technology in their business environment. Use of P2P technology is not encouraged unless there is a strong and exceptional business case to justify its use for file-sharing. In any case, classified or personal information should not be shared in a P2P network.", "bbox": [ 186, 399, 868, 480 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If a P2P network is not required, security policies should be established to block all unnecessary ports. Staff should be regularly reminded not to install P2P applications on the workstation.", "bbox": [ 186, 485, 878, 535 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Traffics in critical networks should be monitored by an IDPS. Any unauthorised P2P traffic detected should be investigated and blocked. A clear firewall policy should be defined to allow the minimum necessary network ports.", "bbox": [ 186, 540, 863, 605 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If use of P2P technology is deemed necessary, the software should be installed to an isolated workstation with dedicated Internet connection and configured with due care, default settings must be examined before use. All unnecessary user privileges and file / directory sharing on the workstation should be removed to prevent exposure of files not intended for sharing inadvertently.", "bbox": [ 186, 610, 882, 694 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10.7 Security Risk Assessment and Audit", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 117, 716, 539, 735 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Security risk assessment should be performed periodically, after major changes and prior to implementation. It is required to be performed at least once every two years. It targets at reviewing the existing security measures and identifying for any potential security vulnerabilities.", "bbox": [ 184, 757, 880, 825 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "header", "text": "OTHER SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS", "bbox": [ 564, 55, 880, 70 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Internet Gateway Security", "bbox": [ 115, 915, 426, 931 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "Page 39", "bbox": [ 821, 915, 880, 931 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "A security audit can be a general review on existing security policies or a technical review by the use of various security assessment tools that should be used with considerable care to scan the host systems and the networks for security vulnerabilities. It targets at ensuring that the current protection mechanism complies with the existing security policy.", "bbox": [ 184, 86, 880, 171 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Audit scope and objectives should be clearly defined to ensure that all target network components are included.", "bbox": [ 186, 192, 847, 225 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Technical audit review should be performed prior to implementation. Host based scanning is necessary for each host in the gateway, especially for the running services and file permissions.", "bbox": [ 186, 230, 838, 280 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Firewall policy should be thoroughly audited for its rules and allowed services.", "bbox": [ 186, 283, 867, 301 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Password mechanisms should be checked and assured for effectiveness.", "bbox": [ 186, 305, 810, 321 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• After audit, testing results and data should be removed from the network components and stored securely.", "bbox": [ 186, 325, 816, 359 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Access should be controlled to prevent unauthorised persons from accessing the scanning tools.", "bbox": [ 186, 363, 875, 396 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Audit recommendations should be followed up as soon as possible.", "bbox": [ 186, 401, 773, 418 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10.8 System Management and Operations", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 117, 440, 542, 460 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• User accounts should be properly managed and maintained.", "bbox": [ 186, 484, 710, 501 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "No users or staff are allowed to install or run web servers or mail servers for Internet access, without obtaining formal approval from the Head of B/Ds.", "bbox": [ 186, 504, 847, 539 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "All roles and responsibilities of staff performing system administration and management should be clearly defined, assigned and documented.", "bbox": [ 186, 542, 838, 576 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Procedures should be well established and followed for the Internet gateway such as change and configuration management control procedures especially for firewalls, backup and recovery procedure, web content management procedure and other related ones.", "bbox": [ 186, 579, 878, 644 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Programs or software installed and run on the hosts should be of secured modes to prevent unintended alteration, and be applied with latest patches or updates.", "bbox": [ 186, 649, 873, 684 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Administration for critical components should be performed directly from a locally attached terminal, otherwise, strong authentication such as tokens, smart cards, challenge-and-response or one-time passwords etc. should be employed.", "bbox": [ 186, 687, 875, 738 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Regularly check online security news or archives, for latest technical advice on security incidents or vulnerabilities.", "bbox": [ 186, 741, 870, 774 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Configuration should be reviewed and modified with respect to the latest environmental changes such as changing requirements, emerging security threats or vulnerabilities.", "bbox": [ 186, 777, 826, 827 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• System welcome, greeting or error messages may disclose internal system information. Disable these messages whenever appropriate.", "bbox": [ 186, 832, 828, 865 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "header", "text": "OTHER SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS", "bbox": [ 564, 55, 880, 70 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Internet Gateway Security", "bbox": [ 115, 915, 426, 931 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "Page 40", "bbox": [ 821, 915, 880, 931 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If possible, install and use management tools or services to centralise system administration and installation, e.g. using software for site-wide installation of patches.", "bbox": [ 186, 87, 865, 137 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "\\*\\*\\*ENDS\\*\\*\\*", "bbox": [ 440, 179, 559, 195 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "header", "text": "OTHER SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS", "bbox": [ 564, 55, 880, 70 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Practice Guide for Internet Gateway Security", "bbox": [ 115, 915, 426, 931 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "Page 41", "bbox": [ 821, 915, 880, 931 ], "page_idx": 45 }, { "type": "text", "text": "11.
